## Final Report

**Best design: b-0005, 2mm single-layer graphite plate.**

My own judgment against the requirement limits from `brief`:
- R1-screen (≤420K, nominal): 400.67K — **pass**, margin 19.3K
- R2-hotspot (≤340K, FE): [335.3104, 335.311]K — **pass**, margin ~4.69K (the FE bracket is only ~0.0006K wide, so this margin is real, not a discretization artifact)
- R3-mass (≤100 kg/m²): 3.6 kg/m² — **pass**, huge margin
- R4-thickness (≤40mm): 2mm — **pass**, huge margin

All four requirements are met. This appeared at evaluation round 2 (the 5-candidate bracketing batch, bringing the budget to 5/12 evaluations used).

At 3.6 kg/m², this is roughly 15x lighter than the lightest passing design in the prior constellation (20mm aluminium at 54 kg/m²), because the prior sweep only explored 10-30mm plates, far past the point where mass matters — the actual binding constraint (FE hotspot) turns out to be satisfiable with a plate an order of magnitude thinner.

**Why I didn't go lighter:** I bracketed the failure knee directly — 1mm graphite fails FE (344.43K > 340K), 2mm passes (335.31K). Since thicknesses must be whole millimetres, 2mm is graphite's minimum viable thickness. I also checked that graphite has the best conductivity-to-density ratio (0.083) of all seven materials versus aluminium (0.074), aluminium nitride (0.052), copper (0.045), and confirmed epoxy — despite lower density — fails catastrophically on the screen (900K) due to negligible conductivity. Any second layer would add at least 1mm × its density in mass, and no non-insulating material is lighter per mm than graphite, so no layered combination can beat pure 2mm graphite.

**What I'd try next with more budget:** Test whether an asymmetric or non-uniform lateral design (not expressible in this layer-stack model) or a different heat-source geometry assumption could relax the spreading requirement further — but within the tool's layer-stack model, I believe 2mm graphite is at or very near the true optimum.
